conventions.convention: The complete-data density is one supplied jointly measurable nonnegative function on parameter, observation, and latent coordinates, normalized on every parameter fibre. Both reference measures are sigma-finite. Separate likelihood versions do not imply joint measurability; supplying the joint function requires no choice axiom.
The normalized latent density p/m is defined only on fibres with 0<m<∞; no quotient is assigned at zero or infinite marginal.

KL uses D(P||Q), with the first measure absolutely continuous with respect to the second for the RN integral formula. AC is assumed; zero divergence characterizes equality of laws. The normalized-density identity additionally requires finite-valued densities, positive finite normalizer, support inclusion, and the displayed absolute log-integrability condition.

Gradient-descent indices start at k=0 and count accepted updates. Stationarity is checked before the caller predicate. Fixed-step domain failure returns the last valid iterate. Rate statements concern generated iterates only.
Damped Newton requires a positive-definite Hessian for its Cholesky solve, tests λ²/2≤ε before line search, and uses 0<α<1/2 and 0<β<1. A stopped iterate has no asserted successor.
The strongly convex rate assumes an attained minimum, 0<μ≤L, and fixed step 1/L. Its power formula is stated for k≥1; k=0 is handled separately, avoiding 0^0 when μ=L.

load_bearing.statement: A jointly measurable latent-variable density is a specified nonnegative product-measurable p(θ,x,z), normalized on every parameter fibre. Its observed marginal is m(θ,x)=∫p(θ,x,z)μ(dz), and q=p/m is defined only where 0<m<∞.

Assume AC. For probability measures P,Q on one measurable space, D(P||Q)≥0, and D(P||Q)=0 if and only if P=Q. For the stated sigma-finite reference measure, finite-valued normalized-density inputs, support condition and absolute log-integrability, log Z=∫q(log γ−log q)dμ+D(qμ||πμ).

Under the latent-factorization hypotheses, m is jointly measurable, each fixed-parameter observed marginal integrates to one and is finite almost everywhere, and every positive finite fibre yields a measurable probability density q=p/m. Fubini exchanges the observed and latent integrals of hp under the stated absolute integrability.

For a continuously Fréchet differentiable real objective on an open Euclidean domain, use the negative gradient with supplied positive fixed steps or domain-aware Armijo backtracking, subject to stationarity, caller-stop and fixed-step domain-failure branches.

At a differentiability point in an open domain, if Df(x)[p]<0, trials start at 1 and shrink by β∈(0,1), and α∈(0,1), then the Armijo line search accepts after finitely many reductions. For the Newton branch, assume the current Hessian is symmetric positive definite.

For continuously differentiable f on all of R^d with an attained minimum, an L-Lipschitz gradient and μ-strong convexity, where 0<μ≤L, fixed-step gradient descent with step 1/L satisfies f(x_k)−f*≤(1−μ/L)^k(f(x_0)−f*) for every generated k≥1; the initial gap is unchanged at k=0.

seams_checked.note: Both pages restrict normalization to finite positive evidence and distinguish supplied joint measurability from separate likelihood versions. The latent construction does not infer a Bayesian posterior or prior-predictive probability from fibrewise normalization.

The EM algorithm and ascent theorem retain jointly measurable normalized complete-data input, positive finite observed fibres, directional current-to-candidate KL, AC, support inclusion and integrable logs. KL nonnegativity is used only for probability laws.

The ELBO and coordinate-ascent proofs use the general probability-law KL nonnegativity clause under AC. They derive their density-ratio identities locally rather than applying the batch's more restrictive finite-valued, sigma-finite normalized-density clause without its hypotheses.

Contextual prerequisite: no listed Laplace or quadrature item cites a batch-23 item. The page supplies its own mode, Hessian, domination and global-gap hypotheses and imports no optimizer convergence guarantee.

Contextual prerequisite: no listed ABC item cites a batch-23 item. Its page preserves finite positive normalization and explicit joint-density requirements without claiming the latent or optimization results prove ABC convergence.
The HMC definition cites the Euclidean gradient and C¹ input convention of gradient descent. It does not import descent, optimizer convergence or Newton guarantees into Hamiltonian dynamics.

ULA uses the fixed-step update map x−γ∇U(x) on all of R^d before adding Gaussian noise. The supplier explicitly defines this map at stationary points. No deterministic gradient-descent rate is asserted for the noisy chain.

4DVAR supplies C¹ objectives on open decision domains and invokes gradient descent with a finite update limit and domain-failure handling. The supplier's caller predicate supports the update limit, and no minimizer or convergence guarantee is inferred.
